records.name: MacGuffin Theatre & Film Company
records.summary: A nonprofit theater company that teaches classes in acting, musical theatre, comedy and film for children and teens, with camps and after-school programs. It also runs troupes for improv, cabaret and acting, and holds auditions for its productions.
records.what_you_do: Take a class during a fall, winter or spring term, sign a child up for a summer camp or after-school program, or join a troupe such as improv, cabaret or comedy. Auditions are held for productions.

schedule.text: Classes run on Wednesdays and Saturdays in the fall, winter and spring terms. The After School Program meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays through the season, and troupe rehearsals are on Saturdays.

cost.text: Troupe tuition on the audition page is $295 for fall and winter and $245 for spring. Class and camp prices are not on the pages read. Scholarships are offered on financial need, and only a limited number are available.

first_step.how: Sign up for a Fall 2026 class through the enroll page on macguffintf.com, or email info@macguffintf.com first to talk through your goals and ask about scholarships.
first_step.basis: The classes page says beginners are welcome and invites a call or email to talk through learning goals, and the enroll page gives a clear route to sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes run on Wednesdays and Saturdays during each term, and the After School Program meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Youth classes are for ages 7 to 10 and middler and teen classes for ages 11 to 18. The pages read do not give class length or term prices, so ask the office before you pay.
first_visit_tips: Auditions are held on the second floor at 2030 Sansom Street, behind a purple door, so look for that door on your first visit.
Ask about a scholarship before you pay. Applications are reviewed on financial need and take 2 to 3 weeks to process.
The company uses an opt-out photo policy, so tell staff early if you do not want to appear in photos or videos.

records.notes: The classes page says beginners are welcome and lists Wednesday and Saturday classes plus Tuesday and Thursday after-school sessions. Age bands: the homepage says teens to 17, the fall page says 11 to 18; the record uses 18, so check. Season changed from fall to year_round because terms run fall through spring and summer camps are offered. One audition listing is dated 2025 and was left out; only 2026 dates are used. Camp and class sign up runs through two outside booking sites linked from the enroll page, and the page does not say whether an account is needed.

records.name: Mad Beatz Philly
records.summary: A percussion education group that teaches drumline to students at schools around Philadelphia and trains young people to become music teachers.
records.what_you_do: Schools book weekly drumline classes for students (the curriculum is aimed at grades 4 to 8), and adults 18 and older can train as music teachers while earning pay for teaching work. The group also books drumline performances for schools, festivals and events.

schedule.text: Weekly drumline classes at participating schools for all skill levels, offered as semester and year-long programs. Students aim to be ready to perform in about 3 months.

locations.label: Philadelphia school sites (8 sites listed as a count, none named)

cost.text: Schools pay a price based on school size and program length, and the site lists no dollar amounts. Teacher training has individual and cohort pricing, also without amounts. Performance prices vary by event type and location.

first_step.how: Call 267-872-4942 on a weekday between 8 am and 6 pm, or use the Book Mad Beatz Philly form on the site, and ask whether a class can be set up at your school or whether teacher training is open to you.
first_step.basis: Classes are booked by schools and programs, and the site does not say individual students can join a class, so the way in for a newcomer is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes run at partner schools, taught by the group's teaching artists, with equipment provided and a goal of performing within about three months. Teacher training is 10 sessions for people 18 and older, moving from apprenticeship to co-teaching to leading a classroom. The site does not describe a drop-in class open to the public.
first_visit_tips: Have the school's staff make the booking request, since the classes are booked through schools.
For teacher training, ask about the pay, the start dates and the 10 sessions before you commit.
The office answers the phone Monday to Friday, 8 am to 6 pm, and the site promises a 24-hour response to inquiries.

records.notes: The programs page aims school classes at grades 4 to 8 and sets teacher training at ages 18 and up. Performance pricing varies and no class days or times are listed. Undated counts on the About page (266 drummers at 8 sites, a recent apprentice cohort) are not used as evidence, and the impact counters show 0, so status stays probably_active with no last_sign_of_life. The named partners Musicopia and the Highmark Mann Center for the Performing Arts have no URL on the pages read, so they are noted here and not in leads_only.

records.name: Malta Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club on Boathouse Row, founded in 1860, that is open to anyone interested in the sport. Members row socially or race, coach and volunteer at Philadelphia rowing events.
records.what_you_do: Row socially or race, use the erg and weight room, or volunteer, officiate or coach at Schuylkill Navy and city rowing events.

cost.text: Dues and fees are not published on the club's site.

access.notes: The erg and weight room is on the third floor of the clubhouse.

first_step.how: Call (215) 769-9030 and ask how a new person joins as a social rower, what the dues are, and whether the club offers a learn-to-row option.
first_step.basis: The club is open to anyone interested, but the site lists no join steps, dues or learn-to-row program, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The club's site describes members who row socially or race on the Schuylkill, and a heated third floor erg and weight room with locker and shower rooms. It does not say how a first visit works, what it costs, or whether a beginner can try a boat, so ask first.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, because the site lists no opening hours.
Ask whether you can see the erg and weight room, which is on the third floor.

records.notes: A web search (the one WebSearch call) found no current dues, joining steps or learn-to-row program for this club. The results were about other clubs, or a listing that says it was generated with AI, so nothing from them is used. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the way in is unclear. The site has no dated items, so status stays probably_active with no last_sign_of_life. No schedule is recorded because the site lists no hours.

records.name: Mama-Tee Community Fridge Project
records.summary: A volunteer-run network of community fridges across Philadelphia that puts fresh food within reach of neighbors. It also runs a pop-up grocery store on Washington Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Help stock the fridges with fresh produce, organize donations, join a school or company volunteer day, or help with projects from home. Volunteers start by sending an email.

schedule.text: Fridges are restocked each week, and anyone can take food from them, first come first served.

locations.label: St. Christopher's Hospital for Children (North Philly)
Opportunity Towers I and II (Nicetown, two fridges)
Community Partnership School (Strawberry Mansion and Brewerytown)
Fridge at a site the page does not name (Germantown)

first_step.how: Email hello@mama-tee.com with the subject line for the track you want: Volunteer Inquiry for the regular volunteer track, Corporate or School Volunteer Inquiry for a group day, or Virtual Volunteer Inquiry for remote work.
first_step.basis: Three volunteer tracks are listed openly with a direct email route, but the page gives no shift days, times or training, so the first shift is arranged by email.
first_step.what_to_expect: Regular volunteers help stock the fridges with fresh produce, sort donations, and connect surplus food with people who need it. Shift times, training and what to wear are not published, so the first step is an email conversation. Fridge food is free and open to any neighbor, and the fridges are restocked each week.
first_visit_tips: Pick the email subject line that matches your track, so the group can send you the right next step.
The fridge locations page marks four fridges as out of order and one as relocating, so check that page before you go to a site.
For the pop-up grocery store at 2203 Washington Ave, call 215-585-2767 to ask about its hours.

records.notes: The tier 1 claim of a Saturday 1 pm pop-up grocery was not on the group's homepage or fridge pages in two reads, so the day and time were removed. Please check it before publishing. The homepage counts (18 fridges, 55 volunteers, 278,502 people served) are undated and conflict with the 16 fridges on the fridge page, so none are used. Zig Zag BBQ, the YMCA, Castellino's and Myers Recreation Center are marked out of order, and 308 N 39th St is marked relocating; these are left off the locations list. The citycast and inquirer links are carried over from tier 1 and were not re-read this pass. Kind changed from program to network to match the batch file. drop_in set to false because volunteering starts with an email; the fridges need no sign up to use.

records.name: Mamadêlê Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts foundation that teaches and performs the music, dance and culture of Bahia, Brazil. Its ensembles perform, it runs adult community classes and youth education programs, and it leads trips to Bahia.
records.what_you_do: Take the free percussion workshop series, ask about adult community classes at Dendezeiros Studio, come to a performance by one of the group's ensembles, sign up for the newsletter, or join a trip to Bahia. Schools in Philadelphia host semester-long residencies.

schedule.text: Classes, residencies and workshop series run on dates posted on the group's events page.

cost.text: The four-part workshop series is free. Class and trip prices are not listed on the pages read, the site suggests donations between $25 and $500 or a custom amount, and private lessons can be arranged by email.

first_step.how: Use the Register Today link on the adult percussion classes page (a Google Form) to sign up for the free percussion workshop series, or email mamadele@mamadele.com to ask about adult classes at Dendezeiros Studio.
first_step.basis: The free series is open to people of all backgrounds and has a registration form and an email for questions, but the pages do not say whether beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The free percussion series is a four-part workshop led by Dendê Macêdo, covering rhythms, movement and history from Candomblé and samba de roda through hands-on practice, demonstrations and conversation. The page calls the series intergenerational and open to people of all backgrounds. Session times and session length are not published on the pages read, so confirm them when you register.
first_visit_tips: Ask about session times when you register, since the event listing does not show them.
The venue phone is 646-361-6918, but the event page does not link it to registration, so use the form or email to sign up.

records.notes: The adult percussion classes page turned out to describe the free workshop series, not a class timetable. Adult class names, days, times, levels and prices were not readable, so none are written. A $200 percussion class item on the education page could not be tied to adult classes, so it is not used. The event page gives the series as October 3 to 11, 2026, with no session times; those dates are kept out of schedule and appear only in last_sign_of_life. The event page labels 646-361-6918 as the venue phone. Registration is described as a Google Form on one page and is not mentioned on the event page. Status is active because of the October 2026 event listing on the group's own site.

records.name: Marconi Older Adult Program
records.summary: A program for adults 50 and older at the South Philadelphia Boys and Girls Club, with a grab-and-go lunch, coffee and conversation, games, crafts, technology classes, fitness, and trips.
records.what_you_do: Come for lunch and conversation, take a tech or art class, join a fitness session, get help with resources, or go on a trip. The program also lists rides and wellness phone calls among its offerings.

schedule.text: Activities include a grab-and-go lunch, coffee and conversation, games, classes and trips. Call the program for the days and hours.

locations.label: South Philadelphia Boys and Girls Club

cost.text: The site does not list a fee. Call to ask about any cost before you come.

first_step.how: Call (215) 218-0800 and ask how to join the older adult program, or send a question through the Contact Us page on caringpeoplealliance.org.
first_step.basis: The program is open to adults 50 and older, but the pages give a phone line and a contact page rather than steps to enroll in the older adult program, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The program offers a grab-and-go lunch, coffee and conversation, games and crafts, art and technology classes, fitness sessions, parties and dances, and trips. The pages do not say how long a visit runs or what it costs, so ask when you call. Rides and wellness phone calls are also listed.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 218-0800 first, since hours and fees are not listed online.
Ask about the program's transportation when you call, because it is listed as one of the offerings.
The program is at 2433 South 15th Street, inside the South Philadelphia Boys and Girls Club.

records.notes: The tier 1 last_sign_of_life of 2026-10 came from a city senior-site list, not a dated program item, so it was removed. The newsletter page lists 2026 items by year only, with no month, so no month is written; status is active on that basis. Two phone numbers appear: the program page gives (215) 218-0800 for the South Philadelphia club and the Marconi program, and the newsletter and main pages also show 1.215.545.5230, which the enroll page lists under Mission Support. The record uses 215-218-0800. The enroll page's Google Form is titled for Boys and Girls Club enrollment, so it is not presented as the older adult route. The full-list page has no activity text, so activities come from the main program page.

records.name: Mayfair Memorial Playground Friends
records.summary: Neighbors who raise money to keep Mayfair Memorial Playground in good shape, and who have run volunteer days and fundraisers since the group formed in 2009. The website's newest dated post is from February 2021, so check before you go.
records.what_you_do: Give money through the donate page, come to a fundraiser, or help on a volunteer day such as the spring cleanup the group has called for in the past.

cost.text: Donations are taken online through the donate page. The site does not say whether the playground charges.

first_step.how: Email the city's Parks and Recreation stewardship office at pprstewardship@phila.gov and ask to be connected with this Friends group, since the group's site lists no way to join or volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site gives no way to join or volunteer, and its newest dated post is from 2021, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group's history page describes neighbors doing hands-on work, such as a 2011 build day with about 200 volunteers and mulching in later years. Recent volunteer days are not listed on the site, so ask by email what is coming up. The playground sits on Abraham Lincoln High School property.
first_visit_tips: The playground sits on Abraham Lincoln High School property, so ask the Parks office where to meet.
The newest posts on the site are from 2020 and 2021, so confirm that a volunteer day is still on before you come.

records.notes: Status changed from active to dormant. The tier 1 active status, with last sign of life 2026-10, came from a city Friends group list, which is not a dated post by the group. The newest dated group post is the February 2021 fundraiser: the homepage gives its date as 8 February 2021, and the post's archive link shows 2021/02. The events page's newest item is an April 2020 spring cleanup. Verdict stays publish because the group is on the city list and its site still works; the orchestrator may want to decide whether dormant groups stay visible. The site's footer shows 2015 as a copyright year and was not used. The street address comes from the city list, since the site shows none.

leads_only.name: Schuylkill Navy
leads_only.note: Named on the Malta Boat Club site as the rowing body whose events the club races and volunteers at; not checked

notes: Batch of 7 groups, all read at the deep level: 30 WebFetch calls (within the 42 allowed for 7 groups), 1 WebSearch (Malta, no usable result). No blocked pages and no rate limiting. Changes to tier 1 fields: Mayfair status active to dormant (no group-dated post after February 2021; the city list entry is not dated group evidence); Marconi last_sign_of_life removed (the old value came from a city senior-site list); Mama-Tee pop-up day and time removed (not on the group's site on two reads); MacGuffin newcomer rating raised from 3 to 4 (classes page says beginners are welcome) and season changed from fall to year_round; Malta newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 (join route unclear); Mama-Tee drop_in set to false and kind changed from program to network to match the batch file. Conflicts left for the orchestrator: MacGuffin age band (teens to 17 on the homepage, 18 on the fall page; the record uses 18); Marconi phone numbers (the record uses 215-218-0800); Mama-Tee homepage counts (18 fridges and 55 volunteers) against the 16 fridges on the fridge page, with undated counts not used. Mad Beatz partners Musicopia and the Highmark Mann Center have no URL on the pages read and are only mentioned in its notes. Mamadele adult class details could not be read, so none are written.
